label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**From: Amaka_Bio100 | 2026-11-08T21:30:00**

Good evening Tolu, and sorry to hear where you are right now. I was in your shoes last year, so I'm going to answer you as honestly as I can, and I promise you I'm not going to sit here and tell you what you want to hear just to make you feel better.

First, the short answer to your last question: **Biology is not a bad course.** I'm actually enjoying it more than I expected, and I'm not saying that to console you. But since you asked for the truth, here's the full truth, including the part that's hard to hear.

---

**How I found out**

I scored 251 in JAMB 2025. I applied for Medicine and Surgery. I got my admission letter, I was so sure, I even told my mother before the portal had finished loading. When I finally logged in and saw "Biology" sitting there in the status column, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't eat that whole day. I remember thinking my life had just been decided for me at 18.

The funny, painful part was that for two months after that, my mother was still going to church and telling people "my daughter is doing medicine." I had to beg her to stop. I didn't want people asking me questions. Please don't let your dad's and aunty's version of your story become the version you tell yourself, because at some point you will be the one in church and they'll be the ones asking you.

---

**Can you actually transfer? Yes. Is it easy? No.**

Kingsley said transfer is a myth. That is not true, but I understand why people say it — because most people who say "I'll transfer after 100L" never actually do the work to get there.

Here is what my level adviser told us, word for word as best I can remember:

- You need a **CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5** at the end of 100L.
- There must be **space** — i.e., the department has to have available slots for the higher level.

And then the part people don't talk about: you also need to **meet the Medicine cut-offs for JAMB and post-UTME** for your own school. Tolu, this is important. Your 268 on its own does not establish your eligibility. The cut-off is a combination of the two scores, and every school weighs them differently. I don't know your school's cut-offs and I don't know your post-UTME score, so I can't sit here and tell you "you qualify" or "you don't." **You must check both.** Go and ask the faculty, or check the admissions office, and get the actual numbers.

My adviser also said something that put things in perspective for me. Last year, from our **whole faculty**, about **six people** were moved into Medicine. Over **forty** had applied. So it is not impossible, but the ratio is not in your favour, and the people who made it were not average students.

And since she asked: **my CGPA after first semester was 4.31.** Not 4.5. I'm still trying to get it up. I'm telling you this so you don't picture this as "sit down, read hard, 4.5 comes easy." I had to genuinely work for it.

---

**What 100L is actually like**

Our courses are **BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST.** Being honest, it's not Biology dragging people down, it's **Physics and Maths.** Most of my colleagues who entered wanting Medicine are struggling in PHY 101 and MTH 101, not in the biology papers. If you're strong in those two, you have a real chance of hitting 4.5. If you're not, that's where your first year will quietly slip away from you.

Money-wise, be ready. These are small things but they add up: **lab coat was 6,500 naira**, **dissecting kit 9k**, and the **practical manual** is separate on top of that. That's before books and ordinary living. Just factor it into whatever you and your family are planning.

One memory I want to share because it changed my mind a bit. Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, honestly he was the first to go down. I was fine. And that was the day I realised something I did not expect: **I actually like this thing.** It's not medicine, but it's real science, and being in the lab, understanding how living things work, doing genetics and cell biology — it's satisfying. I didn't feel that before I got here. I only felt it after.

**Biology is not a punishment.** If you end up here, don't waste the year resenting it. Ifeoma would probably tell you the same.

---

**About rewriting**

I won't tell you to rewrite. I'm in Biology and I'm telling you it's a real place with real courses.

But I also can't pretend rewriting is a free option. My secondary school classmate **Ifeoma** rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has now written JAMB **two more times**. She is still at home. She is not lazy and she is not stupid — she just didn't get what she wanted the second and third time either. That's a real person I grew up with, and I think about her often.

So: **staying at home is not as easy as people say.** favour said you'd see your mates going to school and be depressed, and that's true. I saw it too. But rewriting is not wrong if **you** are ready for it — meaning you can actually sit down and study for another year and come out with a much better score, not just "try again and hope." A 268 is a good score. People score below that and still get into Medicine. But "just rewrite" is easy to say when you're not the one doing it.

And favour's "just read hard in 100L" is too simple. It's more than reading hard. It's 4.5, and space, and cut-offs, and the possibility that you do everything right and still don't get the slot.

---

**What I would actually do in your position**

1. **Go to the faculty/department and ask for the exact transfer rules for your own school.** The full requirements, the cut-offs, who to write to, what the documentation is. Do this this week, not next week. And please do not trust forum people for this — **including me.** I know my school, I don't know yours. Forum advice is free and it is often wrong.

2. **Look at your post-UTME score and your school's Medicine cut-off** and write the numbers down. If you're close, you have a real case for staying and fighting for 4.5. If you're very far, you should think seriously about rewriting while you still have the time.

3. **Ask yourself the question nobody wants to ask:** do I want Medicine, or do I want to be "doctor" for my parents? I am not judging, because I was 18 and I did not know the difference myself. But medicine is not the only path to being a doctor. There are other health sciences, and there are careers in this country where people are doing well and respected without the MBBS. If what you actually want is to help people, the answer might not be the one your aunty thinks.

4. **Don't let the two-week deadline push you into a decision you didn't think about.** The deadline is real, but the pressure is worse. Take the days you have to gather actual information instead of arguments from relatives.

---

**The last thing**

Whatever you choose, **it is not the end of the world.** I know that sounds empty at 19, crying in your room. But I promise you, from someone who was exactly where you are: I am fine. I am in 100L, I am working on my CGPA, I am enjoying genetics, and I still have my whole life in front of me. If I had accepted it and been home for two years instead, I'd be worse off and no happier.

You are not behind. You are not a failure. You are a person who got the outcome she did not want and has two weeks to decide what to do about it, and that is a hard thing, but it is a solvable thing.

If you want, send me your post-UTME score and the name of your school and I'll tell you what I can about how people are doing — but again, please go and confirm with your own faculty, abeg.

And please eat something tonight. The crying stops, the hunger doesn't help anything.

**Amaka_Bio100**
